DISGATE102.topics: Functions and limits; Continuity; Differentiation; Optimization; Taylor series; Complex numbers; Definite and indefinite integrals; Integration techniques; First-order differential equations; Population-growth and predator–prey models; Second-order linear differential equations; Dynamic models

ENSSUST313.name: Research in a Sustainable Delta

Emphasises hands‑on projects in disaster response, sustainable agriculture and environmental monitoring.

options.label: Water, delta risks & quantitative environmental science
options.concept: Study delta water systems and environmental risks through flood adaptation, geoscience, groundwater fieldwork and geochemistry. Use calculus, probability, numerical methods, GIS and programming to analyse environmental processes and data.

options.label: Infrastructure impacts, ecology & environmental governance
options.concept: Study how infrastructure and adaptation decisions affect coastal habitats and communities. Use ecology, geospatial analysis and spatial planning to investigate those effects, and examine public participation, environmental justice, material recovery and renewable energy.

analysis: The water option combines delta protection and freshwater, geochemical analysis, field soils and aquifers, plus programming, numerical methods and probability. Dynamic Earth supports geohazards and runs after the two sustainability gateways but without creating an unmet prerequisite. The second plan studies ecological consequences using biodiversity, ecosystem and marine ecology courses and combines site data, applied spatial planning, public participation and environmental justice. Spatial Planning contributes geospatial projects on disaster response and environmental monitoring, while Earth Observation gives broader geospatial methods and data acquisition. Renewable System Design contributes technical and economic analysis of supply, and Hydraulic or structures design is outside both routes. The two options differ by nine courses each way and have distinct objectives and methods. Advanced Calculus, Earth System Science Tools, Natural Hazards, Earth’s Resources, climate communication, environmental justice, renewable-system design and spatial planning each receive their documented scope in the course-level review. Introduction to Programming, Data Science, Linear Algebra and GIS would support transport study, but available course content does not build traffic demand, network assignment, transport policy or construction-process simulation into a programme.
